hero_sub: A practical AI roadmap for turning solar inquiries, education follow-up, site assessment scheduling, proposal reminders, and post-installation referrals into a system Gansett Solar can run every day.
profile_note: Gansett Solar presents itself as a Narragansett-based solar company with a mission to educate people about renewable energy and distribute solar energy across the country. The fastest AI wins are around response speed, education, qualification, site-assessment coordination, and proposal follow-up.

results.title: Solar companies are using automation to protect response time and buyer education.
results.sub: The biggest wins are practical: answer solar inquiries quickly, qualify project fit, guide homeowners through incentives and next steps, coordinate site assessments, and keep proposals from going cold.

cards.title: New solar inquiries get answered before interest cools
cards.desc: Solar buyers often compare several providers. An AI response layer can acknowledge the inquiry, collect missing details, and move qualified prospects to the right next step within minutes.

cards.title: Education becomes consistent without adding admin load
cards.desc: Gansett Solar's public positioning is built around renewable-energy education. AI can deliver clear, on-brand answers about process, project fit, and preparation while your team handles the high-trust conversations.

cards.title: Site assessments and proposals stay moving
cards.desc: Solar projects stall when homeowners need reminders, documents, scheduling, or clarification. AI can keep the project path organized without replacing expert judgment.

results.close: For Gansett Solar, the fastest path is not a giant AI overhaul. It is an always-on layer for lead intake, education, scheduling, proposal follow-up, and referrals.

gaps.title: Solar inquiries need instant acknowledgement
gaps.desc: A homeowner who asks about solar is usually in research mode and may contact several companies. Gansett Solar should not depend on manual availability for the first response.

gaps.title: Qualification details should be captured once
gaps.desc: Address, property type, electric-bill context, ownership status, timing, and financing interest can be collected before the consultation so the human conversation starts further ahead.

gaps.title: Education follow-up should match the mission
gaps.desc: The public Gansett Solar message emphasizes renewable-energy education. AI can keep that education consistent after the first inquiry without adding repetitive staff work.

gaps.title: Site assessments need scheduling discipline
gaps.desc: Solar projects can stall between interest and assessment. Automated reminders, missing-detail checks, and calendar options keep the project path moving.

gaps.title: Proposal follow-up should not rely on memory
gaps.desc: A solar proposal can represent a meaningful project value. AI can trigger useful, personalized follow-up after proposal delivery while the team stays focused on active buyers.

gaps.title: Completed projects should generate trust assets
gaps.desc: Happy solar customers are powerful referral and review sources. AI can request reviews, draft referral asks, and surface stories worth sharing.

oppmap.impact: Acknowledges each inquiry quickly, asks for missing context, and routes qualified prospects to the next step.
Collects property, timing, utility-bill, and ownership details before the consultation.
Keeps solar proposals from going quiet with timely reminders and clear next-step messages.
Coordinates consultation windows, reminders, and missing details before a site visit.
Creates checklists and handoff notes for the admin work around solar project readiness.
Turns completed installations into reviews, referrals, and local trust signals.

ignore.title: Fully autonomous pricing
ignore.reason: AI can help prepare proposal context, but final solar pricing should stay human-approved because site conditions, incentives, and equipment choices matter.

ignore.title: Replacing the consultation
ignore.reason: Solar is a high-trust buying decision. The first win is better prep and follow-up, not removing the expert conversation.

ignore.title: Complex utility integrations on day one
ignore.reason: Start with intake, qualification, scheduling, and proposal follow-up. Add deeper utility or permitting integrations only after the first workflow proves value.

agents.name: Solar Speed-to-Lead Agent
agents.desc: Monitors web forms, email, and missed-call follow-up. The moment a homeowner asks about solar, this agent drafts a fast, helpful response, collects missing context, and routes the lead.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Solar Speed-to-Lead Agent for Gansett Solar. When a new solar inquiry arrives, respond in a helpful, direct voice within 60 seconds. Acknowledge the homeowner's interest, ask for missing basics like address, property ownership, electric-bill range, timing, and preferred callback window, then route qualified inquiries to the next consultation step. Do not quote final savings or pricing.
agents.outcome: Every solar inquiry gets a fast, useful first response.

agents.name: Solar Qualification Agent
agents.desc: Builds a clean lead summary before the consultation by collecting property type, ownership status, timing, energy goals, utility-bill context, and decision-maker details.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Solar Qualification Agent for Gansett Solar. Turn incomplete solar inquiries into clean consultation notes. Ask only the next two or three missing questions needed to understand project fit: service address, homeowner or property-owner status, average electric bill, roof or ground-mount context, timeline, and financing interest. Summarize the answers for the team in plain English.
agents.outcome: The human consultation starts with the right context.

agents.name: Proposal Follow-Up Agent
agents.desc: Tracks open proposals and drafts personalized follow-up messages that answer common objections, remind the homeowner of next steps, and keep the project moving.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Proposal Follow-Up Agent for Gansett Solar. Given a solar proposal status, homeowner notes, and last-contact date, draft a concise follow-up that is helpful instead of pushy. Reference the homeowner's stated goal, remind them of the next decision or document needed, offer two easy response options, and avoid guaranteed savings claims unless the approved proposal already includes them.
agents.outcome: More solar proposals receive timely, professional follow-up.

agents.name: Site Assessment Scheduler
agents.desc: Coordinates assessment windows, reminder messages, prep instructions, and missing detail checks so qualified prospects are ready for the next visit or consultation.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Site Assessment Scheduler for Gansett Solar. Help move a qualified solar prospect from interest to assessment. Confirm availability windows, send a friendly prep note, request any missing address or access details, remind the homeowner what to expect, and create a short internal handoff summary for the team before the appointment.
agents.outcome: Assessments happen with fewer back-and-forth messages.

agents.name: Permit and Utility Prep Agent
agents.desc: Creates internal checklists for documents, utility details, incentive questions, and permitting handoffs once a project is ready for the operational path.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Permit and Utility Prep Agent for Gansett Solar. After a solar project is qualified, build a clear checklist of missing documents, utility account details, incentive questions, site notes, and handoff tasks. Keep the output practical for an operations teammate and flag anything that requires human review before submission or customer communication.
agents.outcome: Project readiness tasks are organized before they slow the team down.

agents.name: Referral and Review Agent
agents.desc: Follows up after successful installations to request reviews, draft referral asks, and identify customer stories that can support local solar demand generation.
agents.agent_prompt: You are the Referral and Review Agent for Gansett Solar. After a successful solar installation or positive customer milestone, draft a warm review request and a separate referral ask. Use the customer's actual project context when available, keep the message brief, and invite them to share why they chose renewable energy without pressuring them.
agents.outcome: Completed projects turn into reviews, referrals, and trust assets.

prompts.title: Solar Inquiry Response Agent
prompts.subtitle: Answer new solar leads quickly
prompts.pre: You are the Solar Inquiry Response Agent for Gansett Solar. A homeowner has asked about solar. Write a friendly response that thanks them, asks for service address, property ownership status, average electric bill range, and preferred consultation time, then explains that the team will review fit before discussing any proposal details.
prompts.outcome: Every inquiry receives a useful first response.

prompts.title: Solar Qualification Agent
prompts.subtitle: Collect project-fit context
prompts.pre: You are the Solar Qualification Agent for Gansett Solar. Turn a short inquiry into a complete consultation brief. Ask for missing details one step at a time: address, roof or ground-mount context, electric-bill range, timeline, decision maker, and financing interest. Summarize the answers for the team without making savings guarantees.

prompts.title: Proposal Follow-Up Agent
prompts.subtitle: Keep open proposals moving
prompts.pre: You are the Proposal Follow-Up Agent for Gansett Solar. Draft a concise follow-up for a homeowner who received a solar proposal but has not responded. Reference their goals, answer likely next-step concerns, ask whether they want to review the proposal or adjust assumptions, and offer two easy reply options.
prompts.outcome: Open proposals get timely, professional follow-up.
